item.content:encoded:
I am not of the opinion that one should be forcing ideas down authors' throats. Experienced authors do not equate always to high level work. A work is high in quality when the authors writes about the subject-matter they care about.

Simply forcing ideas down them when they might not necessarily be onboard with it does little good.

While contests and challenges exist to give limitations and impose ideas, they tend to be of the author's volition.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I was thinking about it earlier, man.

Like, containment personnel have to be swapped out regularly and frequently wind up on medical leave because of liver problems.

"You don't understand, man. I can't remember the last time I woke up without a hangover. I've gained 12 pounds since joining the 3999-J containment team. That fucking thing doesn't let us keep regular hours, doesn't let us sleep. Ever. The music is CONSTANTLY blasting and when the lights are off, strobes come on. Jeremy had to get a fucking liver transplant three weeks after joining the crew. Three fucking weeks, man! I've seen three cocaine overdoses in the last two months. And don't even get me started on what it subjects the ladies to, man."

"Why don't we just send D-Class in?"

"They tried."

"And?"

"It knows. Somehow, it can tell the difference between someone straight-laced, who's never broken a rule in their life, shows up to work on time and stays after-hours, someone who's valuable, and someone disposable like that. And containing it becomes way harder if we just feed it with D-Class."

"Fuck, man, I had no idea."

"…if they try to rotate me back in, I'm jumping off the balcony."

item.content:encoded:
I enjoyed this. Theatre of the mind, given material like that, very much a fun read. For some reason I think Delta-1's use of "de-escalation tactics" (Address the anomaly with authority. Firmly request it cease hostilities and remit itself to containment.) was particularly good.

Plus plenty of other amusing bits. So that's a solid +1 from me.

Say… How about, like, a Saturday morning timeslot for some spin-off show action?

SCP-3999-J ...
... with The Chief as Himself

Site-42 OFFICE INTERIOR, DAY

Director Lyceus and Researcher James Talloran stand in the office of the Chief of Security. The Chief gestures in frustration at the documents spread across his desk.

Folksy Narrator: Well, it looks James and the gang have done it again.

Chief: Surely you see there must have been undue expenditures-

Lyceus: Settle down Chief! This man is a hero.

Talloran grins modestly

Lyceus: Come with me, son. I know this must be a demanding assignment for you; I'd like to discuss some potential avenues of compensation for your dedicated spirit.

Talloran: Thank you sir. Truly it's an honour to serve this cause.

Lyceus and Talloran exit the office. The door closes behind them

The Chief shakes a fist in the air and bellows angrily

Chief: TALLORAAAAAAAAANNN!!!
